results.reasoning: Driven headless at e453e79 on scratch machines (HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME under /tmp/judge8-*), with no server. The base steps hold. A home's path registers that blueprint alone with its ID and project. A repository's path lists each folder, marks the listed one, and registers the numbers picked at a real terminal (driven with expect). With no terminal it lists to stderr, registers nothing and exits 2, and --json keeps stdout empty. --all and --only register; an unknown --only name is refused alike either way. Re-import says already listed with the row unchanged, under /tmp, /private/tmp, a symlinked checkout, or any letter case. Paths holding no home say so. Moves still work, and so do the fixes from n-0522 through n-0541: one home or --only after a move, an unrelated repository at the old path, a shallow clone deepened and then moved, an orphan branch, and zed/shop against acme/shop. The rule fails because import takes rows from a checkout that still stands. ~/shop has three registered homes and its origin URL changed by `git remote rename origin upstream && git remote add origin <fork>`. A plain retargeting, or a trailing slash added to the same URL, does the same. Importing one home from a second clone of the original repository then re-points all three of ~/shop's rows at the clone and prints that ~/shop 'no longer exists'. Afterwards `walkdown status` in ~/shop says nothing is registered there. checkoutGone now treats an origin that differs at the old path as another repository before it looks at the home still on disk. The same script at 24f32ba leaves ~/shop's rows alone, so this is a regression of this fix. A second, older defect also breaks the already-listed step. Importing a home that only a worktree holds registers the worktree as its own project. The worktree's copies of the checkout's registered homes then lose their already-listed mark, and --all registers them a second time as 0005-0007. 793988a does the same.
